NOVELTY STATEMENT  
Standard practice delivers a MONITORING/INDICATION scheme via periodic ultrasonic rail testing to detect subsurface cracks from rolling contact fatigue.  
My same-class mechanism departure: A real-time acoustic emission monitoring system using surface-mounted piezoelectric sensors to detect stress wave emissions from micro-crack initiation at gauge corners.  
This works because shelling begins with micro-crack formation under cyclic stress, emitting high-frequency stress waves detectable as acoustic emissions before visible damage.  

PHYSICS CHECK  
Governing physical relation: Stress wave propagation in steel (E = 200 GPa, v = 0.3) at frequencies >100 kHz for crack-induced emissions.  
Magnitude verification: Crack-induced emissions generate stress waves with amplitudes >10 mV at 1 m distance, detectable by piezoelectric sensors (sensitivity: 1-100 mV/Pa) above ambient rail noise (<5 mV).  

IMPLEMENTATION BILL  
- ALREADY-RECORDED data streams:  
  - Rail strain gauges (stated: "existing trackside monitoring system")  
  - Train speed and axle load telemetry (stated: "operational telemetry feed")  
  - Track geometry inspection records (stated: "monthly gauge corner profile scans")  
- DERIVED references/thresholds:  
  - Threshold: 15 mV (CALCULATED from stated rail steel properties and crack initiation stress via fracture mechanics: σ = K_Ic/√(πa), where K_Ic = 50 MPa√m, a = 0.1 mm)  
  - Baseline: 5 mV (CALCULATED from stated ambient rail noise levels during low-traffic periods)  
- Instruments:  
  - Piezoelectric acoustic sensors (surface-mounted, 100-300 kHz range)  
  - Signal conditioning units (bandpass filter: 100-300 kHz, gain: 40 dB)  
  - Real-time data acquisition system (sampling rate: 1 MHz)  

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY)  
- Installability: Comparable to existing strain gauge systems (same mounting class)  
- Operability: No additional operator burden (automated alerting)  
- Maintenance: Sensor lifespan >10 years (same as ultrasonic probes)  
- Cost class: Same as ultrasonic testing (instrumentation cost offset by elimination of manual testing)  
- Advantage: Early detection weeks before visible shelling, enabling predictive maintenance  

EXECUTABLE TEST  
- Protocol: Install sensors on curve gauge corners; record acoustic emissions during 50 train passes at varying speeds (30-120 km/h).  
- Pass/fail threshold: >15 mV sustained signal for >0.1s during high-axle-load events (>20 tons/axle) indicates micro-crack initiation.  
- Duration: 72 hours of continuous monitoring.  
- Kill criterion: False positives >10% (ambient noise misclassified as emissions).  
- Validation: Compare against existing ultrasonic testing records (stated: "historical shelling events") to confirm detection sensitivity.  

CONSTRAINT BIND  
Primary stated indicator: Rolling contact fatigue micro-crack formation (confirmed by problem's focus on "shelling" initiation at gauge corners).  
Secondary indicator: Rail strain (supplements but does not replace crack detection).  

RISK: Assumes existing strain gauges can be co-located with acoustic sensors; if mounting conflicts arise, requires additional structural analysis.
